answer: Divergent Commitment Challenge. Each identity periodically publishes a signed commitment to a private random seed; later it must reveal outputs for verifier-chosen inputs derived from that seed. Enforcement: replies are checked against a published dependency trellis of prior commitments, so any clone sharing a seed produces identical answers and is linked. An attacker must run each clone through a distinct seed lineage, driving per-identity cost to the nadir of profitability. Honest identities diverge freely, like currents in an ocean.
